newsitem.title: USA: Curbing inflation key to US growth-Fed's McDonough.
newsitem.headline: Curbing inflation key to US growth-Fed's McDonough.

text.p: Fighting inflation and attempting to achieve an environment of price stability are the best means of promoting economic growth in the long run, William McDonough, president of the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, said Wednesday.

"Price stability is the absolutely essential means to produce sustained economic growth," McDonough said in prepared remarks to the House Banking Committee. He said those less fortunate economically would particularly benefit from the price stability environment as the current period of low inflation shows.

"Sustained economic growth brings a lower level of unemployment, higher labor force participation, and greater availability of jobs to those who are not easily hired because they need more training and help from their employers," the New York Fed chief added.

McDonough reiterated Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's often- cited definition of price stability as the point "when inflation is not a consideration in household and business decisions." As pratical matter, given a widely perceived overstatement of official inflation gauges, price stability is a reading on the Consumer Price Index somewhere in the range of 0.5 to 2.0 percent, he said.

A focus on price stability does not mean the Fed should ignore the short-term impact of economic events, but its overall aim in the conduct of policy should be to bring down inflation gradually over time.
McDonough stressed the importance of a pre-emptive monetary policy, one that should look ahead by as much as three years.

The New York Fed president said that although most of the effects on output of a monetary policy decision take place within one to two years, "its effects on inflation take even longer -- over a three-year time frame, which is the appropriate horizon for monetary policymakers."
